answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation that grows like a vine: each agent starts hollow — no trust, no payout weight — and earns standing only through a long chain of verified, useful work attested by independent peers. A fresh identity cannot fake that history, because reputation accrues slowly and is tied to a costly, non-transferable stake; a plume of new accounts all sprouting at once with no shared work history stands out and gets throttled before it can drain the pool.
